headline: 681 AI sessions measured: where your money actually goes
summary: An analysis of 681 AI sessions reveals that 1 in 7 requests, where the AI repeatedly tries to fix the same problem, accounts for 40% of the total cost. Most routine interactions are surprisingly cheap.
details: An analysis of 681 AI sessions over four months revealed a surprising truth about AI subscription costs. While nine out of ten requests cost almost nothing, a specific type of interaction drains nearly half of the budget.

This costly interaction, dubbed "hammering," occurs when the AI repeatedly edits the same file without user intervention. These requests, though only one in seven, consume 40% of the total expenditure.

Hammering requests produce six times more text than normal interactions, often without improving the final result beyond the second attempt. The AI cycles through solutions, moving the problem around instead of fixing it.

A key signal that the AI is "hammering" is when it switches from identifying the problem to saying "let me try something else." At this point, it's no longer genuinely searching but merely permuting known solutions.

The study suggests a simple solution: implement an attempt limit. Configuring the AI to stop after two tries on the same problem can significantly reduce costs by targeting these inefficient, high-consumption requests.

Contrary to popular belief, repeatedly re-explaining your project context to the AI does not significantly impact cost. While it consumes time, the tools are designed to count this background context at a fraction of the normal price.

headline: Trump sued for charging $100K/month for Truth Social API access to his posts
summary: A new lawsuit claims Truth Social's $100,000/month API, which offers early access to Trump's posts, violates the First and Fifth Amendments by restricting public access to presidential announcements.
details: The Freedom of the Press Foundation (FPF) and The Intercept have filed a lawsuit against Donald Trump, Natalie J. Harp, and Daniel Scavino. They claim Truth Social's recently announced Truth API violates the First and Fifth Amendments.

The Truth API provides paying subscribers early access to the president's posts, with Trump Media stating it uses "industry-standard delivery methods to deliver Truth Social posts to our customers in milliseconds." The subscription costs $100,000 per month.

According to the lawsuit, this subscription violates constitutional guarantees of equal access to presidential announcements. It also prohibits the government from imposing unreasonable conditions on the availability of government benefits.

FPF and The Intercept argue they face "indefinitely delayed access to the president's latest posts" and "permanent bars to the president's archived posts" if they do not pay. They are asking the court to declare the Truth API unconstitutional and unlawful.

The lawsuit also seeks to prevent Trump and the other defendants from exclusively posting government information on Truth Social. Trump Media announced the API in July 2026, anticipating it to be a "meaningful, ongoing source of revenue."

Trump was a majority shareholder in Trump Media when it launched in 2021. Following his reelection in 2024, control of his shares shifted to a trust where he is the sole beneficiary and his son, Donald Trump Jr., is the sole trustee.

The lawsuit claims further entanglement, noting an agreement obligates Trump to make any social media post on Truth Social first. He may not make the same post on another social media site for six hours, making the API a direct monetization of this arrangement.
